title: Warmup latency probe oddities — personal investigation journal
content:
Summary:
This is a running scratch/journal of experiments and breadcrumbs while investigating repeated capacity thrash and long tail cold-starts in the Dedicated GPU pool serving the 'v2-text' family. Behavior: autoscaler briefly provisions nodes, pods schedule but spend 30–90s with GPU idle before the runtime is ready to accept inference requests. End-user latency spikes and downstream request queues pile up.

Key symptoms observed (high-level):
- Spikes in request queuing on route /v2/generate between 09:10-09:27 UTC on 2026-03-01.
- Pod startup time (kube-scheduled -> ready) observed: median 22s, 95p 78s.
- GPU memory shows zero usage for ~20–60s after pod 'Ready' state (nvidia-smi shows processes only after runtime reports ready).
- Autoscaler then observes low util and tears nodes down, causing repeated thrash.

Timeline / breadcrumbs (local notes):
2026-03-01 09:05 - alert triggered: route SLO > 3s, queue length 120
2026-03-01 09:07 - looked at events: kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
  Found multiples: "FailedScheduling" transient, then "SuccessfulCreate" events.

Commands and outputs I ran (copied snippets):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide | grep v2-text
  v2-text-5657   1/1 Running   0   32s   10.1.12.42   node-pool-gpu-7

- kubectl describe pod v2-text-5657 -n redwood-serving
  Events:
    Normal   Scheduled   3m   default-scheduler   Successfully assigned redwood-serving/v2-text-5657 to node-pool-gpu-7
    Normal   Pulled     2m   kubelet   Successfully pulled image "gcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.3.4"
    Normal   Created    2m   kubelet
    Normal   Started    2m   kubelet
    Warning  Unhealthy  1m (x3 over 30s) kubelet   Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500

- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving v2-text-5657 --container=runtime
  [INFO] loading model weights from /models/v2-text/quantized/part-0.bin
  [INFO] kv cache init: not primed
  [WARN] grpc: connection not ready: context deadline exceeded
  [ERROR] readiness: model init incomplete: cache priming pending

Hypotheses so far (ranked):
1) Model image pulls and startup hooks are fine; main delay is model weight mmap/quantized load + kv-cache population. Runtime marks pod Ready before the low-level readiness (we have two readiness checks?). Mismatch between Kube readiness probe and runtime readiness semantics.
2) Node/driver GPU initialization is fine, but driver warmup (CUDA context + cuBLAS init) + one-off kernel JITs cause long first-pipeline latency and runtime holds readiness until cache primed which takes variable time depending on sequence length / tokenizer warm-ups.
3) Autoscaler config is too aggressive on scale-down/unneeded eviction thresholds (scaleDownUnneededTime default 1m). Combined jitter causes thrash when loads are bursty.
4) Cold KV-cache priming depends on live traffic; if no synthetic warmers run, the first request pays full cost and readiness/probe interplay causes additional churn.

Experiments attempted (commands + results):
A) Increase readiness probe timeout to 120s on canary deployment (k8s patch):
  kubectl patch deploy v2-text -n redwood-serving --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/timeoutSeconds","value":120}]'
  Result: fewer readiness failures but median provision time still high; 95p reduced slightly (78s -> 64s). Autoscaler still tear-downs after spike.

B) Pre-pull image + precreate device context via initContainer (attempt):
  Added init container that runs nvidia-smi and python -c 'import torch; torch.cuda.init()' to pre-init driver context.
  Observed: small improvement in first-log timestamps; model load still dominates. Noted initContainer consumes extra node startup time ~6s.

C) Local script to prime kv-cache by sending short inference probes after pod Ready: prime.sh -> curl /v2/ping; curl /v2/generate with small prompt.
  Result: when priming runs, subsequent readiness transitions show lower tail. But priming requires access to route (service) and fails if autoscaler removes node before prime completes. Race remains.

D) Temporarily raised dedicated pool min size to 4 (was 1) to avoid scale-to-zero during bursts.
  Result: incident quieted; latency SLOs recovered. Cost impact obvious but mitigated risk.

Interesting logs and oddities I captured:
- Node kubelet logs show sporadic delays creating device plugin sockets: "Error: timed out waiting for /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins" but no OOMs.
- Runtime logs: "kv cache init: not primed" appears in 100% of cold starts; time between that line and "runtime ready" varies from 3s to 92s.
- Observed sequence where pod reports Ready but readiness probe behind the scenes returns 500 for 15s; event ordering suggests Kubernetes thinks Ready earlier than runtime surface indicates.

Quick trace (hand-timed):
- Node becomes Ready: t0
- Pod scheduled: t0+3s
- Image pulled: t0+18s
- Container started: t0+22s (kubelet sees started)
- runtime logs: model load begins at t0+23s
- runtime signals READY (HTTP /health) at t0+85s
- kubelet readiness check sometimes passes earlier at t0+40s (inconsistent)

Questions to validate / next steps: 
- What exact readiness endpoint does Kube probe hit? Is there a mismatch between /health and /ready semantics in the runtime? (Action: grep templates + helm values for readinessPath).
- Can we make the runtime surface two endpoints: /probe/startup (fast, reports container up) and /probe/serving (reports model & kv primed)? Then ensure kubernetes uses the serving readiness for routing but the startup one for liveness only.
- Could we implement a deterministic cache priming step in the image entrypoint that runs asynchronously and blocks readiness only until model artifacts are mmapped? Tradeoff: adds node startup time but reduces tail variance.
- Autoscaler tuning: raise scaleDownUnneededTime to 3m and add a burstBuffer of 2 nodes to reduce thrash. Test on canary.

Quick TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Confirm exact readinessProbe settings in current helm chart (infra repo PR 856). (Ethan assigned)
- [ ] Add explicit 'model-ready' endpoint to runtime to remove ambiguity. (engineering spike)
- [ ] Run a synthetic warmup job that attaches to service IP and primes tokens during node provisioning (prototype in tools/warmers).
- [ ] Experiment with keeping 1-2 permanent warm nodes for the busiest pools (cost vs SLO tradeoff).

Notes on hypothesis validation:
- If priming is the main cause, then a synthetic priming step should cut 95p startup from ~78s to <20s. My crude local prime cut the worst cases to ~18s in 3/5 tests.
- If kernel JIT is dominant, then repeated JITs should show up as occasional longer spikes even after priming; need to measure CPU/GPU profiler (Nsight/rocprofiler) during the 1st request.

Commands to reproduce warmup locally (notes for QA):
- kubectl apply -f debug/warmup-pod.yaml -n redwood-serving
- kubectl port-forward svc/v2-text 8080:80 -n redwood-serving &
- ./tools/prime-client.py --host localhost:8080 --prompt "hello" --repeat 5 --sleep 0.5

Random breadcrumbs / side-observations: 
- Observed one node with slightly older nv driver which took an extra ~20s in first JIT; need check node image drift across pool.
- Memory usage of runtime binary during load peaked at 1.2x steady-state (expected) then dropped as segments swapped in. No OOMs.

Decision log (temporary):
- 2026-03-03: Raised min pool size to 4 to stop immediate user impact. Will revert after deeper fixes or will move to permanent small warm pool.

Closing note: this is messy, exploratory, and partial — left here as a personal breadcrumb trail for follow-ups. If you pick this up: start with the helm readinessPath check and then run a controlled prime experiment (tools/prime) while instrumenting runtime for exact timestamps between 'mmap done' and 'serving ready'.

-- Maya
